reader.requirement: At --std 85 data-name-1 of START ... KEY may be written qualified (by any chain of containing group or record names, IN or OF, and by the file-name), and the qualified reference must resolve to the unique item it names, an unqualified or wrongly qualified ambiguous reference being refused.

reader.notes: BindStart resolves data-name-1 through the shared qualified resolver (ResolveSending, QualifierWalk with the file-name arm) and RecordKeyNameOf; every qualification form 1985 prints resolves and both refusal forms are diagnosed. The edition is consulted on the path only for neighbouring rules (85-only INVALID KEY requirement, 2002-only subscripted operands). The ambiguity and SR4 messages cite 2023 clause numbers (cosmetic).

refuter.evidence: Probe r3start-001 at --std 85 (two indexed files sharing key names KEYF/ALTK, keys declared qualified in the SELECT, a second record REC1B redefining the prime key with a shorter KEYF): START IF1 KEY = ALTK OF G1 OF REC1 -> A1 00 K003MM03 (alternate key qualified by two levels); START IF1 KEY > KEYF OF G1 OF REC1B with K00 -> INV-2 23 (truncated comparison makes no key greater, §1985:IX.4.7.4 GR4); NOT LESS -> A2 00 K001ZZ01; START IF2 KEY NOT < ALTK OF IF2 (file-name qualifier, sequential access) -> A3 00 J002AA02; KEYF IN REC2 -> A4 00 J002AA02. r3dgrp-001: a 3-byte group GK OF REC1D OF IF1 at the key's leftmost position -> G1 00 K001ZZ01 (SR4b, 1985 group is alphanumeric). r3bref-001 refusals: KEYF OF G1 (ambiguous) COBOL1639; ALTK OF IF2 and KEYF OF REC2 in START IF1 COBOL0862; subscripted GT (1) and GT OF REC1B (1) COBOL0862 (data-name-1 is a data-name at 85); KEYF OF IF1 in START IF2 COBOL1639. r3clate-001 class c: WITH LENGTH, KEY IS LESS THAN, KEY <=, START FIRST each refused COBOL0900 requires COBOL-2002. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.7.3 SR2; OK §1985:IX.4.7.4 GR4; OK §1985:IX.4.7.3 SR4b.
